correctness.rationale: Every full sweep equals a composition of one-dimensional saturating affine responses; the clipping identity yields an exact map T(z)=clip(B+(-1)^n W z;L,H), with all coefficient and range recurrences proved. A contraction argument handles W<1. At W=1 an increasing translated clipping map settles finitely and the odd decreasing map squares to a projection. Above gain one the increasing clipped-affine map has a unique expanding affine root and exact absorbing plateaus: every orbit is fixed after finitely many iterates. This applies to T for even n and to T^2 for odd n, where the at-most-three fixed points imply at most one two-cycle. Rational recomputation verifies 53550 compositions, 510 critical tests, 6480 supercritical orbit samples, and four examples; these finite checks supplement a full proof.

originality.rationale: Section 3, Example 3.2 of the fully inspected arXiv:2101.03863 gives a 0–1 cycling witness and parity observations, while Section 5, Example 5.1 and Theorem 5.5 give contraction/spectral-radius sufficient convergence. For a directed weighted cycle the latter covers W<1, which is explicitly credited. Neither those statements nor the relevant main proofs assert the heterogeneous all-initial, all-gain clipped-affine phase diagram, supercritical finite-time convergence for even rings, or uniqueness of primitive two-cycles for odd rings. The new theorem follows from separate complete return-map calculations. Search comparisons found no equivalent specialized claim; a prior unlocated treatment remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Directed public-goods games are a motivated setting where symmetric-network convergence does not apply. The exact gain/parity phase boundary, unconditional finite stabilization for supercritical even rings, uniform period-two ceiling for all odd-ring trajectories at unit or higher gain, and uniqueness of supercritical cycles resolve a complete natural parameter class left between the source’s isolated cycle example and weak-influence sufficient convergence theorem. The structural mechanism is explicit, constructive, and holds with heterogeneity. The result is not a free reformulation of the prior sufficient theorem.
